work_units.notes:
CDFChart.tsx:103-115 uses `L` (lineto) to connect CDF points, producing
smooth diagonal lines.  A true ECDF is a step function: horizontal
segment to the x-value, then vertical jump to the next cumulative
fraction.  The Python reference (textcharts.cdf_chart) renders steps.
Visual divergence is minor on dense data (22+ queries) but visible on
sparse distributions.

Fix: render H→V steps instead of diagonal L commands.  No math change
needed - computeECDFPoints output is already correct.
work_units.summary: Render CDFChart as ECDF steps, not smooth lines
Data-gate Histogram / Box Plot / CDF tabs in BenchmarkIndex

work_units.notes:
chartRegistry.meta.test.ts:19-36 - CANONICAL_IDS is a third hardcoded
copy of the chart type list (alongside chart_types.py and chartRegistry.ts).
The test detects TS-side drift but NOT Python-side drift: if someone adds
a 17th type to chart_types.py without updating the test's list, the test
passes.

Fix options:
  (a) Parse chart_types.py at test time using Node fs.readFileSync +
      regex to extract chart IDs from _CHART_SPECS.
  (b) Emit a machine-readable chart-ids.json from the Python pipeline
      as a build artifact and compare against that.
  (c) Accept the current triple-write but add a comment warning that
      chart_types.py is the authority and all three must be kept in sync.

Option (c) is the lowest friction; (a) is the most robust.  Avoid (b)
since it couples the static build to the test suite.
work_units.summary: Replace hardcoded CANONICAL_IDS in meta-test with dynamic chart_types.py parse
